I see - the `_match_re` uses `^%s$`. The issue with trailing newlines is that `$` in Python regex (without MULTILINE) matches at the end of the string OR just before a newline at the end. This can cause issues when you have a trailing `\n` in your input.

For example, if format is `{x}` and input is `"hello\n"`:
- The regex would be `^(?P<x>.+?)$`
- With `re.DOTALL`, `.` matches `\n`
- But `$` will match just before the final `\n`, so it might try to match only "hello" instead of "hello\n"
